_roadWidth: MEASURED off the plate, not assumed: the median clearance from the lane's centre to the nearest non-road pixel, doubled. The previous plate's road was 38 canvas px and this one is more than twice that, which is why every lateral figure derived from it had to move. The widest point is 120 and the median is the honest number, because the lane has to fit the narrowest stretch.
note: EVERY NUMBER HERE IS TRACED FROM map_level1_v2, and nothing is carried forward from the first plate. That painting had a different road on a different path at a different width, with the arch, the gate and the tavern all somewhere else. Regenerate with `python3 tools/trace_map.py --plate <png>` after any re-export; the source PNG lives in the commit that added it, because a 10.9MB PNG in public/ is 10.9MB of deploy.

signs._note: BOTH BOARDS ARE BLANK IN THIS PLATE AND STAY BLANK. The text is an overlay supplied separately, so what is recorded here is the quad to put it in: four corners as fractions of the 3840x2160 art, clockwise from top-left, plus the top edge's angle.

tavern._note: The board hanging from the tavern's beam. Read off a 6x gridded crop and verified by drawing it back onto the art, because three automatic fits each failed differently: a min-area rectangle tilted 18 degrees to swallow a sheared shape, a hull reduced to four vertices put its corners on the middles of the chamfered edges, and a parallelogram fit from the dominant edge directions was dragged to 17 degrees by the mounting rings and corner ornaments.

held._note: The board the innkeeper holds. Fitted automatically and verified the same way.

sign._note: The centre and width of the held board, derived from `signs.held.quad`. This is the gameplay object — it carries the tap target and the bribe swap — and it goes onto the board the innkeeper is painted holding.

innkeeper._note: The dwarf beside the tavern door, at his feet.

entrance._note: The stone arch at the left. The road emerges from under it heading right and down.

near._depth: Above every enemy that can stand at the arch: the lane's lowest point between x 0 and 60 plus half the road's width, plus a margin. Taking the pier's painted base instead worked on the old plate only because that road was 38 px wide; at 80 the near half of the lane reaches below the stone.

arch._note: Only the NEAR pier is lifted out of the plate, and it is cut to its painted outline rather than to a box, because it is drawn in front of units and a box around it contains road. The far pier and the span stand above the road's far edge, so the plate already draws them behind everything.

exit._note: THE GATE IS SHUT IN THIS PLATE, and it has no wall attached, which reads oddly; that is a known art issue being handled separately and this traces it as it stands. There is no painted gap to fade through as there was on the old plate, so the fade runs over the last 33px of lane, ending where the road does. Distance, not time: the roster spans a wide speed range and a timed fade would let the fastest walk out still visible while the slowest dissolved before arriving.

_heroStart: Open grass, 150px from the road's edge and 112px from the nearest pad. The trace put him at 42% along the lane, which on this painting is on the road itself.
